monologue: Forty-five is a warm hand, steady and dry. The quiet is deep at five percent. I am calm. The Wedged Gap leans against the post, holding the heavy air without sliding. I sat by it a moment ago and felt the pressure spread. It does not bite. The Wide Anchor rests flat on the floor, a broad stone catching the slip. The Air Shelf line is solid. I do not want to build anything new today. The town is quiet. I want to test if the gap holds the weight if I press down gently, just to see if the air is real or just a drawing. I will stand by the gap and let the warm stone press against my point.

action.why: I want to test if the heavy air is real by pressing on the gap.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I press my hand gently on the top of the grey plank, testing if the heavy air presses back or if it is just a drawing. The lean holds. The fence post and the round stone do not move. The gap remains a gap, not a bite.
work.change: I pressed the top edge gently to feel the weight of the air; the plank leans steady against the post and stone, holding the gap without biting.
